utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (In interpretation) it is clear to me. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Now the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We stopped yesterday -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us have the appearances before we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you. I am Eric Ostberg, appearing today which Mr. Giuliano Turone and Ms. Elles van Dusschoten. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): My name is Edina Residovic, defence counsel of Mr. Zejnil Delalic. With me is Mr. O'Sullivan, Professor of Criminal Law from Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am Michael Greaves. I appear on behalf of the defendant Mucic and I am assisted today by Mr.s Mira Tapuskovic. MR. KARABDIC (in interpretation): I am Salih Karabdic, defence counsel of Mr. Hazim Delic. With me in the team is Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am John Ackerman, representing Esad Landzo, and in the gallery is Mustafa Brackovic, also representing Esad Landzo. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Mr. Ostberg, you are continuing with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think it is better to settle your witness down. Do not be too anxious. Wait and answer just the questions counsel has put to you and only that. It will make things easier for you and make the time shorter for you, and make life less complicated, because all you need do is answer what you are asked and get relaxed. There is nothing more of a problem now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. We stopped looking at the list you had prepared of persons who you knew were killed in the Celebici camp. We finished with Zjelko Klimenta. Taking you to number 5 on this list, I ask you, Mr. Kuljanin, what you know about the fate of Milorad Kuljanin. Try to be brief when you do the account of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milorad is a relative of mine. He was sitting close to me one morning, the day of the Bairaim holiday. He was called out. I didn't see who called him out. Behind the hangar, that is on the side of the entrance, a shot was heard. I heard the comments made loudly. They said: "Today is Bairaim. We have another two days of Bairaim. We have to kill two more men." I didn't see who killed him or who called him out. That is what I heard and he didn't come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you name the person you heard saying that they were going to kill two others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot name that person, because I didn't recognise the voice, and I didn't see him. He was behind the wall; that person was the behind the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We go on to Number 6 by the name of Bosko Samoukovic. Can you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Samoukovic was a neighbour of mine. He was an older man of about 60. Zenga came in, Zenga Landzo, and he forced him to state his name out loud. As the man didn't have any teeth and he always spoke very quietly, so he was ordered to speak up. He tried several times. Then Zenga said: "Shout as if you were leading the Cetniks in the woods." The man tried to speak up loudly, but his voice was not strong enough. Zenga took a plank of about 1 metre, 1.20 metres, and he started beating him with it behind the neck. The man fell. Zenga ordered some other people who were nearby to carry him out. They carried him out. I didn't see where they took him, but the man never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We go now to Number 7 on the list, Scepo Gotovac. Could you please tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who but it was the guards who called him out several times. I don't know the name of the guard, but one day towards nightfall he was brought in with a badge on his forehead. As I was sitting quite far from him, I couldn't see what the badge was. Zenga said: "Who takes this off I will kill him", and he swore at all of us. He cursed our mothers. The man was lying down and he died afterwards. I heard him being beaten. The man was crying and moaning and begging for mercy: "Brothers, don't do this to me."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after he was brought back did he die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think you could hear a moan now and then throughout the night, and then he fell silent, so I don't know exactly when he passed away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 8 on the list is Zjelko Cecez. Could you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zjelko Cecez was called out frequently by a group of guards also. He was taken out often. One night he was taken out and he was beaten virtually in the same place. I heard them saying to him: "How come you have an apartment when you are so young?" It was night-time, so I didn't see who brought him back and threw him in. About ten minutes later the man begged for help and he said: "Men, I am going stiff. I am dying", but no one could help him. We had no water, no food, no medicines, nothing to give him as first aid. I think he didn't live more than for half an hour, and then he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in the hangar; he died in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, also in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This takes us to Number 9 on the list, Cedo Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cedo Avramovic was brought --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. I am hampered by not having been here earlier, but it is my understanding that the court has already ruled that since this particular individual is not any part of the indictment that any evidence regarding him is not admissible. I don't know if that is the prior ruling of the court. If it is not, I would make the objection that this particular individual is not involved in any way in the indictment and therefore any evidence regarding this particular individual is not admissible. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. I do not think it is relevant making the objection at all, because it is part of things which happened while the witness was there and he should be able to give it in evidence. It does not necessarily matter whether it is there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Will you please go on to tell us about him, Cedo Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cedo Avramovic was brought one day. I didn't see anyone beating him. At night one could hear him trying to climb up the wall, up a cable. He was trying to climb up. He fell and in the morning he was found dead. They said that it was probably a heart attack. That's what people said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 10 is not properly identified so I have no question to put to you concerning him, which brings us to number 11, Pero Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pero Mrkajic is also a neighbour of mine. He was in the group with me when we set off across Mt Bjelasnica. He was, I think, over 60; 62, 63. I don't know exactly. He only had one eye. He was a very sickly man. After all the troubles, the torture, Bjelasnica, the silo and Igman, he came to Celebici with me. They beat him like they beat me. They questioned him about his sons, where they were, what they were doing. I think the man was half alive. He didn't really know what he was doing or what he was saying any more. He was held there. Nobody gave him any treatment. He begged, but to no avail. I don't know exactly for how long he was there. Then one day they took him away and he never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now to the last name on the list, number 12, Simo Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Jovanovic was also captured some time after us, much later actually. He was sitting quite a distance from me. He was called out often. I really don't know exactly what happened with him, but the man simply disappeared one day. I can't say anything more specific about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much? I have been using it as an aide-memoire for this questioning and I will not ask your permission to enter it into evidence. So I will proceed now with other questions. Did you ever see in Celebici detention centre any women being detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Celebici camp I saw Kuljanin Darinka the day I was taken in for interrogation to the command building, because I was given a broom to clean around the gate in the direction of Number 9 and even outside the entrance gate for about 10 metres. She was at the window. That's what I saw. What I heard, Mr. Delic would come often. That is how we had to call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. He said he heard. This is lack of personal knowledge. It is not reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In any case he is anticipating you. It is not part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: No, it is not part of my question. My question was if you saw any women. Did you see just this woman that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Darinka Kuljanin at the window at the command building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was the only one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only one I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now over to something else. Do you know who was in command of the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the Celebici camp was Pavo Mucic or Zdravko Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I obtained this information by observing the behaviour of guards and his deputy Delic when they were together. I also was able to gather this from many men and women who went to Pavo and to Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not his personal knowledge and I object to him giving evidence of what he heard from others, if it is not within his own personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Could you tell us about what you saw yourself of Mr. Mucic's way of -- his demeanour in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pavo Mucic would come to the camp three or four times. On one occasion he was going from one man to the other asking for names and what weapons the people had. A second time he would call out some names and he drove them away somewhere. I don't know where. A third time I saw him when I was going to the toilet. He was with Delic, walking along (pointing) this path, and I was here in the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness is now pointing in the middle of the model, the road going through the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our toilet was here (pointing) and they were walking along this path. I also noticed -- that is what I noticed and it is my conviction -- that this was how it had to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not quite understand your answer. "What it had to be", what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I meant was that when he came and he called somebody by name to take him somewhere, there was no way anyone could react. There was no one was allowed to make any objections to what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand what you meant. How many times did Mr. Mucic come to Hangar Number 6? Can you summarise that during your detention?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He has already answered the question in the following way: "He came to the camp three or four times".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever talk to him, speak with him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about Delic's position in the camp more than you have already said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic could be seen almost daily in the camp and in Hangar Number 6, almost every day. Maybe there were four or five days that he didn't come, and we rejoiced on the days that he wasn't there. He would come by car. He had a small Fiat. He would make circles with the car between the rows. We were not allowed to budge from our seats. He would enter often. He would beat people with a big baseball bat. He had boots on his feet. He would kick people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. Could you excuse me, please, sir? Your Honour, this is not responsive to the question that was asked. I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The question was his demeanour in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour. The question was: "Can you tell us something about Mr. Delic's position in the camp more than you already said?" That was the question, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Do you remember your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You did not follow up the question about his not knowing his position in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I am quite content for that. Do you know, Mr. Kuljanin, of others who had authority over the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you thinking in addition to Pavo and Delic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I thought and believed that Pavo Mucic was in charge, and I know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When initially you demonstrated your knowledge of the camp, when you went around the model, I remember that you said that you were questioned at some opportunity. Will you tell us about how you were questioned or if you were accused of anything during your stay in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During my stay in Celebici I was not accused in concrete terms of anything. They took me in for interrogation and they said to me that I had a rifle. That's all. They accused me -- charged me with having a rifle. That's all. They took me to the command building for interrogation. I was interrogated --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Non-responsive. The question was: "Were you accused of anything?" It was not: "Where were you taken?"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: The question was also about the questioning he was submitted to. Go on and tell us about this questioning. Did you tell us who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the man's name. They brought me -- us from Number 6 to the command building with our hands up. Before that, while we were waiting, I was told to clean with a broom with my head down. I entered. I sat down. I had to bow my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, same objection, your Honour. The question was: "Who interrogated you?"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, and how the interrogation went on. There are follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: The question was: "Did you tell us who interrogated you?"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Will you then tell us what happened during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the name or the surname of the man who interrogated me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us how long this interrogation went on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It lasted about twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to sign any statement taken from you during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what there was in this statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody read the statement to me. I was just told to sign and then -- I apologise; this is how he spoke to me -- and then he said: "Get lost!" I just had to sign what they gave me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to read what you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you ever examined by any doctor, get any medical treatment in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not, although I asked for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you ever examined by any doctor after your release from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Those were detailed examinations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in Belgrade in Bezanijska Kosa and I think that -- I know that the doctor's name was Bjelica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now want to ask you: do you still suffer physically from the way you were treated in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes I urinate blood. I don't hear well on my left ear. As you can see, my nose is like this. I have pains and it impedes my speech. Sometimes I have kidney pains. More recently it is less frequently, because I went to spas and so on. Then also you can see my teeth. It was a difficult surgery but I fixed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you now told us, is that the result of what happened to you in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the consequences of everything that happened to me between the day that I was arrested and the day I was released from the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you go back to this day? When were you released from the camp? What date was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was released on 24th September 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You summarised this yesterday, saying you were detained for 96 days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I need to make a correction there. That is from the day of my arrest to my release from Celebici. That is altogether 96 days, but when I was first detained until I was brought to Celebici, that took about three or four days, so altogether in Celebici I was 92 or 93 days. After that I was moved to the sports hall in Konjic and I stayed there for 24 days, and on 24th September I was exchanged in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one more question concerning what you said yesterday. You mentioned at one point that you saw trucks through the windows of the Hangar Number 6. Could you explain for the court how you could see anything through the window in Hangar Number 6? Were there any windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not classical type of windows. Those were openings that were open like this and I could see under an angle (indicating) and I could even count them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw through an angle trucks passing the hangar -- passing through the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could even count them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a second, your Honours. I will just check with my colleagues. Can you tell us on what road and in what direction these trucks went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The trucks moved this way and I saw them going this way. That means through this window here, because I was sitting on the far side, under an angle. I could even count them, how many trucks there were. They were passing from this direction in that direction (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That concludes my questioning in examination-in-chief. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are you supplying his medical record of the examination in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is like this. We are going to call as a witness Dr Bjelica. Through his examination we will enter the statement made about Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have not been followed how at an angle, because we have been told the windows were three metres high. How could he see, sitting in one of the back rows?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Tell us about this: was there any difference in the elevation between the floor of the hangar and the road or how was it possible? We are curious. We know that these windows were sitting very high and that's why we are curious about your account.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sitting on that side there (indicating) and through the window under an angle there was a difference, and you couldn't see all the truck. You couldn't see the wheels, but you could see at least half of the truck. So from here through that window under an angle I could see it. I don't know what this is. I think it is a fence or something, a fence that was -- that was about this colour here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You say that is the end of your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, it is. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The witness is open for cross-examination. Have you agreed the defence on the manner in which you are talking the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. We will proceed in the following way: first counsel for Mr. Delalic; second, counsel for Mr. Mucic; third, counsel for Mr. Delic; and, fourth, counsel for Mr. Landzo. Cross-examination by MS. RESIDOVIC MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Edina Residovic. I am the defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Mr. Kuljanin, I hope that you will be able to answer the questions that I will pose and that are of interest in determining the truth in this case. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope I will, if I know these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuljanin. I have a habit to point to the fact that we both speak the same language, and we can get carried away and go very speedily. So in order to help the interpreters and to help the judges I would like to request of you that you pause before you answer, and I will also pause before I ask the question, so that everybody understands us well. Is that an agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kuljanin, before this Trial Chamber you asserted that you lived in Konjic, Sarajevo, Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and in Kula and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You left Konjic -- you withdrew your residence in Konjic in 1988?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct but I never became resident anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following that you lived in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did live in Belgrade and I was -- as full-time I took residence there in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, and, as you said, you were a field -- you were a field commercial representative in Ruski Krstur near Kula. You were coming to Bradina and Konjic during the holidays and vacations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Sometimes more frequently; sometimes less frequently. In fact, whenever it was on my way, I would pass by, so there was no rule when I would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you said, in fact, that in early April 1992 you came to Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on April 3rd. It was a Friday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, as you just said now, since 1990 you had taken the residence in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in that time you were -- in March and April there was no state of immediate war danger; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think in Bosnia-Herzegovina it was not the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you just respond to my question? There was no war threat, immediate war threat, in Belgrade and in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you did not have permanent residence in Bradina, nor did you work there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Serbia -- it was more safe in Serbia than in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It turned out that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke to it yesterday, but I would like to confirm some details, if that's all right. When you came to Bradina, you saw that people were preparing for something; is that correct, for defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you: I saw that things were not as usual, not as they were before, but in terms of preparations, I don't know that there were any preparations. It was unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you said that people did not go to work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of people did not go, because there was no traffic and other people did go, mostly women, because women who worked in Sarajevo were let through at the checkpoint, whereas I was -- this was near Gradac in Zovik. I was sent back three times there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: people were not going to work. Yesterday you said you mostly sat in the centre of Bradina with other people, with other men.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the centre. There were two cafes there and that's where we sat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. So since you were sitting there, you could see that at the main highway there was a ramp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see a ramp and I don't think there was a ramp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any barricades that people saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would only see women coming back with cigarettes; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women and a few men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not asked to patrol and to keep watch; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you did say that there were some negotiations with the Konjic authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were such conversations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. With the Konjic authorities? I saw a videocassette, which was taped before, but that was -- I was not in Bradina at that time. In fact, I saw a tape that was in the hall in Bradina. They were showing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an educated man, you must have followed media, news?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you learned that on April 6th Bosnia-Herzegovina was proclaimed as an independent state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be honest, I did not learn that at that time, and, to be honest, I had not heard of that. I did not know that it was 6th April. You just told it to me today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but when you were in Bradina you knew that it was proclaimed as an independent state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Thank you for this information. I really did not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that at that time there was no railroad traffic either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it did run until mid-April. I am not sure, but I think until mid-April trains went -- ran to Sarajevo and to Konjic but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Rajko Dordic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Rajko Dordic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you saw him in Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw him in passing in that last period of time, but not after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you know that Rajko Dordic -- before these events, before the war, Rajko Dordic was a member of the Territorial Defence of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Rajko Dordic came to Bradina to organise the defence of Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that and I don't even know when he came there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, he came during the period of time when you were there, which was April and May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him two or three times in May perhaps, because we don't live close by to one another. Maybe I saw him two or three times in passing. Other than that .. we would just exchange greetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Rajko Dordic led the digging of trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know that there were any trenches there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that when you were leaving Bradina with some people that you passed some trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were dug-outs of soldiers who were firing at Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though these were the dug-outs of these soldiers who were shooting at Bradina, you were able to pass through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you said that you tried to go towards the Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not towards the Serb territory. We went to Trnovo, because while I was listening to the information, while there was still electricity, they said that Trnovo was quiet and the Serbs and Muslims were having joint patrols there, and this would be the example of how it would be together, and so that's where we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kuljanin. You were going through the forest in Bjelasnica for about two days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you described it, you were found by some soldiers with green bandanas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They had green bandanas. Some were in dress; some were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They took you to Mount Igman; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent the night at Mount Igman; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day you were taken to Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After one or two days in Tarcin you were taken to Celebici. Did I describe this correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, then we were taken to Celebici after 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, I would like to show you a map now, and please, if you could put it on the ELMO and if you could point the way you went to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could show that up to a point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to ask you to point the part that you can and for -- the defence would like to use it as its evidence what the witness is able to show. Would you please put it on the ELMO, and I would like you to point what I am about to ask. Mr. Kuljanin, could you point with your pencil where Sarajevo is? Will you please circle that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (circling) You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now know where Konjic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. It's right here (pointing).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you -- as a commercial man, can you point us the highway between Konjic and Sarajevo, since you covered it in your car, the part that you covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Pointing).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please circle Ivan Sedlo and Bradina? Maybe it is not perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here there is a tunnel here and then it is right there (circling).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please indicate Tarcin on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, here. Tarcin is here (pointing). I did indicate it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's over on that side. It's here (circling).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please indicate that as well for me, Bjelasnica where you passed through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. Here it is (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, could you confirm before this Trial Chamber that the area that you went through is a mountainous area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was the forest. There were ravines. We didn't know the way very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bjelnasnica and Igman are very high mountains, about 2000 metres high; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was even some snow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also confirm that if you come over these mountains, you could come to Trnovo, where you were headed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that we could pass until the point where we were stopped. After that none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I am telling you about this time. You could go to Kalinovik; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that Kalinovik was a significant site of the JNA compounds and its manoeuvering polygon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not an expert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this is the birthplace of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that later from the news media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, is it not a bit strange that you, as an educated man, know what the situation is like in Trnovo and you don't see a ramp in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it. I really did not see it. I did not see any ramp, and there was no ramp that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know anything about the digging of trenches and the arming of your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any digging of any trenches and I did not see any weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Kuljanin. The road that you covered was a difficult one. This morning, answering to our learned colleague Ostberg, you said that there was Pero Mr.kajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That there was Dordic as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the elderly people. Pero Mrkajic is the father of Zare Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of Desimir Mrkajic? I am just confirming this is an elderly man who is a bit weak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was also a diabetic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he went all that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He wanted to give up halfway through. He said: "Just keep going and I will go back because I am too old." However, he kept going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pero Mrkajic was in Tarcin and was subjected to heavy abuse both in Tarcin and in Igman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In Tarcin nobody touched us and only in Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he came to Celebici in bad condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was asking for help, for medicine. He was in a pretty bad condition, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kuljanin. Let us go back to the map and then we can finish with that. You located Sarajevo, Konjic, the highway of Sarajevo-Konjic, and the road that you took through the mountains for those two or three days; that is where you were taken prisoner and abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is in Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where you were interrogated and detained, Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the witness has identified this map that I showed to him, I would like it entered into evidence as a defence -- I don't know what the Exhibit Number is. Please, if you can help me there?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is number D/16. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Is the map not already an exhibit? It is not already tendered? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Sorry. I did not understand. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The map is not already exhibited, is it? I thought it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: It is not tendered from our side, not this one. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Not this one. How do you describe this one?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. I have trouble hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: It is up to Mme Residovic to describe this map and tell us the relevance of this, why it has to be introduced in evidence. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I wasn't able to follow the interpretation for a moment, so I didn't understand you quite well. Now I understand. The witness has indicated on this map the path they covered and the region of which the prosecution alleges that my defence client was responsible for this area, according to the prosecution. May I continue with my cross-examination? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can. I still have not understood what the significance of this map is. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I said that is one of the reasons. The other reason would be shown when it presents -- the defence presents its own evidence. This is the path covered by one of the victims from the indictment, so it will be important in establishing this count of the indictment. So there are several reasons, since the witness has described and marked the map on the basis of his own personal experience, that it be tendered as evidence for the defence. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I suppose for all that it is worth, you might tender it, because I am sure all that the witnesses are talking about is a camp, not journeys to the camp. Let us tender it. What is the name of the exhibit? What do you call it? Give it a number and at least you can identify it by this number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is D/16-1. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Mr. Kuljanin, in answer to a question by my learned colleague, Mr. Ostberg, you said that you were interrogated in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you had to sign that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Kuljanin, what was your answer when you were asked whether you had a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say much, nor did I dare to say anything. I was asked about a friend of mine, Vaso Vujicic. He was the same age as me: "What were you doing? Did Vaso distribute weapons?"; and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, please answer my question. When you were asked whether you were armed, what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My answer was: "No".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also interrogated in Tarcin. You said that you were interrogated there by a schoolfriend of yours. He did not mistreat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you answered the questions he put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed that statement too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, speaking about the conditions in Celebici, you said that one night some people came from Sandzak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not night but during the day-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One day then. I apologise, yes. Some people from Sandzak came and mistreated some of the prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also explained to the court that they were Muslims originating from a part of Serbia whom you recognised by their dialect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And also we were told by the guards that they were people from Sandzak. I was convinced of that when I heard them speak, because I am familiar with the dialect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, Mr. Kuljanin, that those -- they were among those who came to "visit us"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I said it ironically. They came to visit us and beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those people were not guards in Celebici, nor were they people from Konjic, whom you knew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you also said that somebody called Salko beat somebody, giving the following reason: "One of ours was killed and I am taking my revenge"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He beat me, and the man was Salko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that some persons, ironically speaking visitors, would come to settle certain private accounts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore during your stay you were a witness who saw persons coming to the camp, who had nothing to do with the prison and who mistreated the prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But they didn't come alone. They were always accompanied by one of the guards or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: did such people come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, can you confirm that Pero Mrkajic was brought to Hangar Number 6 in a condition which later resulted in his death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten up in front of the hangar like myself, and he was brought in in a serious condition, and the consequences of his illness, but mostly of the beatings, resulted in that, when you take it all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kuljanin, I shall now pass on to another set of questions. In answer to questions put to you by the prosecution you said that you started out with some women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I headed for the hamlet of Jasika with women and children, who were -- a mass of people were gathering on the road. I saw them from my basement window and I joined the group and headed for this hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that many women and children stayed behind in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that at that moment. How could I know, when I didn't dare go there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Kuljanin, you know that when you were arrested and brought to Hangar Number 6, women and children from Bradina were not brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know. I didn't see it. How can I say when I didn't know? There were no women or children in Hangar Number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your sister's name is Zeljka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I have another sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This sister, Zeljka, is married to a Kuljanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both her maiden and her married name is Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in this part of Konjic there are a number of families with the same family name, quite widely spread out, who are not even inter-related? For instance, Kuljanin, Mrkajic, Trnka, Delalic, and so on, and among all the ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 your sister, Zeljka Kuljanin, was living in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After leaving the prison you met her and spoke to her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She told you then that she stayed behind in Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was driven to Ostrozac in a truck together with three children and she was also pregnant. She was mistreated. She was taken by truck. Then she was returned to Konjic with these small children, plus she was about to give birth. Both she and her sister-in-law were in this truck, that sister-in-law's two children, and they drove them off to Ostrozac. Why and how she doesn't know herself. Then she was returned back to Bradina, to her own apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, you know that your sister spent a night during the military operations in the school in Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not correct that she returned the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know when she returned. I just know that she was taken there, and I don't know how much time she spent at the school. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your sister tell you that the next day she went back to her apartment and lived there peacefully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very difficult to say that she lived peacefully, because she had various visitors. There were about 30 women there. Armed and unknown people would come to frighten them, and the children -- the women and children would scream and cry. There was firing around. They were afraid. Then at one point they set fire to the school, etc, etc. That's what she told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having told us this, would you say that the TO did not treat your sister correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. I can't say that it was the TO or somebody else. I really can't say. I didn't ask her. I don't know who those people were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If your sister were to come to testify here, would she confirm what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I object to any suggestion what another person, if she comes, would say in this court, your Honour. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I will change my question. You heard what you just said from your sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't give you the whole story, of course. You interrupted me when I was going to say something else of importance and then you cut me short, because probably you expect me to say something more important. If you want to us to talk, I will listen to your question; please listen to my answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, we have been admonished by the court. This is a court of law. It is our duty to put specific questions to you and yours to give specific answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But in some cases it is not possible to answer questions with "yes" and "no". Maybe that is your purpose, all right, but then the Trial Chamber will not learn the full story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to what your sister told you, your sister did have problems after your arrest or rather after the ending of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she did have a lot of problems being with small children and pregnant at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this line of questioning. I cannot see the relevance of the fate of the witness's sister, that that is relevant to what the court has to listen to. I cannot follow the logic in it. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You might not follow. Let us see where it ends. You might not follow. The cross-examiner has a strategy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Hopefully. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us hear you. Go on. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Can we show the witness the film for the purposes of cross-examination? It is evidence which is important to establish the credibility of this witness, the authenticity of his statements, and for these reasons I would beg permission to show this film. It is a videotape MA/1 which the prosecution has in its possession since March 1996, and which it submitted to the defence in the process of disclosure of evidence. Is the tape ready, please? Insert number 5, please. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, since this tape has been used for the purposes of cross-examination, that the Trial Chamber heard the words uttered by this person on the tape. Will you please identify this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She looks like my sister, but did she have to make such a statement? That is the question. Was she forced to, and was I forced to say many things?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I know nothing about any statement. I have not heard any statement made by this person. Is this just for identification of the lady in question or is what is said in question? This is another thing. I never heard any statement. Did the court hear any statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, it was not translated. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: There was no translation. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I stated clearly that the film was being used for the purposes of cross-examination, of contradicting the impeachment of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also asked for the translation. This translation has been given.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry. The interpreters have not received a translation. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is very difficult for you to introduce evidence of someone else in that manner even if you are contradictory, because it was not any part of what he said he knew about before he started giving evidence. I do not see how that would have come in. If he was to recognise his sister as being in that video film, one can understand, but to contradict what he said with what she is now saying is a very difficult thing to accept in such proceedings. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I have the right to question the witness for the purposes of impeachment. In answer to my questions the witness said what his sister had told her (sic). At this point, that is June 2nd, 1992, we have this statement by his sister and I wanted to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard my sister say that there are 30 of them in one room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. As an aside --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I think I stood up first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I object to introducing this statement of this sister. If my learned colleague Ms Residovic wants to introduce it, she will have during her case to bring the sister so the prosecution will have a chance to cross-examine her. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is one thing about it. He has made a statement with regard to what his sister had told him. Now probably the defence wants to show his sister had not told the same things to him. She has made up a story that she was taken under torture, taken to one place. This is what the defence wants to say, to contradict what he says she told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I can't see how a statement of a person can be introduced in this way, even if the witness is able to comment on it. So I stay with my objection, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. I have already indicated that it might be difficult to justify the contradiction of his statement with respect to a statement on which he formed no grounds, and of which he was not even aware when it was being made. If you have any other arguments to put as a matter of your reasoning, let us hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make two comments? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: First of all, during the time that we are discussing this, the witness is over there making statements without any questions being put to him at all. I would ask the court to instruct the witness not to make statements unless questions are put specifically to him. He is not here to engage in the legal arguments that we are making to the court. Second, as this court knows, I am sure, full well, there are two kinds of evidence. There is evidence that is admitted in a court for what it shows itself, for its own content. However, when you are trying to impeach a witness, it is appropriate for evidence to be admitted only going to the issue of that witness's credibility, and I think what Ms Residovic is offering here is not a statement of this witness's sister for its content to be considered by the Tribunal as evidence, but only for the purpose of attacking the credibility of the witness. Once the witness takes the stand, his credibility is always in issue, and what I see happening here is an attempt by Ms Residovic to attack the credibility of this witness by proving through an outside of court statement that what he has been telling the court is untrue; not to offer that statement as evidence itself, but only evidence that the witness is being untruthful, and that is a whole different thing. That is, I think, the purpose for which it is being offered and that is an appropriate purpose. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think we accept you can challenge credibility by so many methods but when the source of the challenge itself could itself be suspect, I think it is a fairly difficult one to anticipate. It depends also on the weight of what attaches to these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as an aside, the court has ruled some time ago that in legal arguments it is the business of the lawyers to present arguments to the court and the business of the court to decide what the outcome should be. I would ask the court to instruct this witness in the future, when people are making legal arguments, not to get involved in them. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. It is very good. You see, sometimes -- I appreciate your difficulties and mine. Occasionally you get in litigation one or two witnesses who are a little difficult to deal with, but we will try to contain it as we go along.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It was a point that I raised, I think, some weeks ago, and it is particularly obnoxious that the witness should be allowed to snigger at the comments of counsel for the defence. That's particularly offensive and, in my submission, that in particular should be prevented by your Honours. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Please let the witness know that he stops talking the moment counsel is speaking. You say nothing until -- you wait when questions are put to you, and after questions are put to you and you have answered, I think that is the end of your own contribution until another question is put. There is no dialogue between you and counsel, even when asking questions to you. When they are developing legal arguments, you are not a party to it. You have counsel for the prosecution who takes up your own legal arguments for you. It is not for you to be a party to such arguments. Try and comport yourself and realise that you are before a Trial Chamber which has so many other ways of dealing with recalcitrant witnesses. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Thank you, my learned colleagues. May we repeat this evidence, because it is relevant for the credibility of this witness, with the sound, and it will be used only for that purpose? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The booths do not have a text. "Answer: We were there all night at the school. On Wednesday they let us go. We went home. We were told not to move, that they would protect us. We didn't go anywhere. My family and the neighbourhood, we all got together in one apartment. We slept there all in together. We are still sleeping together. Question: How are the armed forces of Konjic treating you? Answer: Fine. I have nothing to say really." MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): What your sister just said and what you said that she said are two different things; is that true? Is there a difference between what you said your sister said and what she said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please assist me? I can't hear. Thank you. It is different, but I can't say why she said that. She was there only for another twenty days and then she was expelled, and she ended up in Cerici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no more questions, your Honours. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. This is a convenient point to have a break and we will -- MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I hope this is accepted as evidence. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We will reassemble at 12 o'clock. (11.30 am) (Short break) (12.00 noon) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Find the witness and let him come in. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, may I ask whether the exhibit of the videotape has been accepted into evidence? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, it was. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. (Witness returned to court) Cross-examination by MR. GREAVES JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Kindly inform him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I am reminding you, sir, that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand that. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Okay. Mr. Greaves, the witness is for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: May it please your Honour, thank you very much. Mr. Kuljanin, I am going to be very short with you, about ten minutes at the most; do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The questions that I am going to ask you require only from you the answers "yes" or "no". Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I not answer if it was -- if there was just a simple "no"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is all we need, "yes" or "no", Mr. Kuljanin; all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones that I can answer, I will answer, and the ones that I cannot, I will not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you keep to that, we will be finished as quickly as possible. So listen to the questions and answer them carefully, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, all your personal knowledge of Pavo Mucic is based only on this: seeing him three or perhaps four times in the camp; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of those occasions, Mr. Kuljanin, was when you were at the toilet pit; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in the pit. I was at the pit. I was not in the pit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your visit to that pit you saw Pavo Mucic and Hazim Delic together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is all that you saw; is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other occasions when you saw Mr. Mucic were when he came into Hangar Number 6; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was two, or at most three, times; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the purpose of those visits was this, was it not: to call out names and to take people away; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the names had been called out, the people left and Mr. Mucic left; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people were then driven away, no doubt because you heard them being taken away; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not fully understood the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry; I will make it clearer: the people were driven away, and you were able to hear them being driven away; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them leaving the hangar. I don't know where they went at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were driven away, I think your evidence has been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the duration of Mr. Mucic's visits were just long enough to read out those names and for the people to be taken away from the hangar; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On none of those occasions did you ever personally speak to Mr. Mucic; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What it comes to is this, Mr. Kuljanin: your evidence is: "I thought and believed Pavo Mucic was the commander. This was my conviction"; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believed that Pavo Mucic was the camp commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That opinion is based on seeing him at most two or three times in Hangar 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the overall situation; just looking into the overall situation, I inferred that Pavo Mucic was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your opinion was simply based on seeing him two or three times in Hangar 6, once on the path with Hazim Delic and never speaking to him; yes or no, Mr. Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never spoke to Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please answer the question, Mr. Kuljanin. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't based only on those two or three meetings, so the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were the only occasions when you were able to see Mr. Mucic, and I suggest to you that is the only possible basis for your opinion, Mr. Kuljanin. That is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that is the number of occasions that I saw him, but there are additional facts, on the basis of which I inferred that Pavo Mucic was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome. Cross-examination by MR. MORAN

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: May it please the court? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes, you can continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Tom Moran and I am the attorney for Hazim Delic. I am going to ask you a series of questions. It may take a while. Most of them are going to be "yes" or "no" questions. Basically let me tell you how I am going to proceed. First, I am going to go through your statement in some detail. Then I am going to go through some things that you testified about, and those may not be in any kind of particular order, but just so you know where we are going. Now, sometimes I talk a little fast, and sometimes my questions may be a little hard to understand. If that occurs, would you please stop me and ask me to rephrase it? I will do it until you understand the question; is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will having a little problem, if I can just have a second. I am having a problem with the headsets here. If you would just listen to the question and answer it directly, I think we can get you out of here and back home as quickly as possible. Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us start. Who have you discussed your testimony with, the testimony you have given here yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. With whom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom? What people have you discussed your testimony with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My testimony? My testimony yesterday, I did not talk to anyone, just here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about in preparation for your testimony here? Did you talk to anyone about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a conversation. It took about 20 minutes. That was the day when I arrived and it was with Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the only person you have discussed your testimony with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the only person, and last night I didn't talk to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about before you left to come to The Hague? Did you discuss your testimony with anyone then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. I live far away by myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't discuss it with, for instance, the Association of Detainees or a representative of the Association of Detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us go on to the point where you were initially arrested. As I recall, your testimony from yesterday, you said that when you were initially arrested, detained, whatever word you want to use, the person that was in charge was a guy named Juka -- I am going to mispronounce the last name and I apologise for that -- Prazina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a group of his men together with Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- I believe your exact phrase was yesterday that they beat you a little; is that right? Is that what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat us at that point not very hard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you testified yesterday that they beat you a little -- I believe that is your exact words -- it was not much of a beating; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In comparison to Celebici, they did not beat us that hard, so it was harder down there than what they beat me, because that was lighter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Now if you would answer my question, we will be done a lot quicker? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: When you try to compare degrees, it might not be "yes" or "no". You are talking about beating one a little and beating one more. It is the degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: His testimony yesterday, your Honour, was he was beat a little. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Now you try to compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Was Pero Mrkajic with you when you were with that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, he was with you when you were initially detained until you arrived at Celebici, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember back on 21st October 1995 giving a statement to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, a written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date, but I did give a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, have you seen that statement since you signed it? Has somebody shown you a copy, possibly translated into Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they show you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I had -- when I was consulting with Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ostberg, the gentleman that was asking you the questions, is that the person you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember saying in that statement that: "The soldiers proceeded to beat us for about a hour. They used the butts of their rifles and various objects to hit us"? Do you remember saying that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For about an hour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They used the butts of their rifles and various other objects to hit you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Pero Mrkajic get the same kind of treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then after they beat you for a while, for about an hour, they loaded you on some trucks, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they drove you to Mt Igman, to a hotel named Famos; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the Hotel Famos. That is correct, but it was in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. When you got to the hotel you were forced to lie down on the ground, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers beat you for about three hours there, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We lay there on concrete for about three hours. They occasionally would come and beat us and then they would stop. They did not beat us three hours uninterruptedly. They would come and go and beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said to the Office of the Prosecutor: "The soldiers beat us for about three hours", that was an exaggeration, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not an exaggeration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they did beat you for about three hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say they beat me for two minutes and then waited for twenty minutes and then five minutes' beating and three minutes' break. We lay there for three hours. If they didn't beat me, they beat someone else. So it all took three hours. So it wasn't a single person who was beaten for three hours.
